the triple-alpha process has the potential to be a powerful test of the Standard Model of Particle Physics.

the triple-alpha process can tolerate shifts in the light quarks mass and the electromagnetic fine structure constant of ≃ 2%–3%, and that it is unlikely that the development of life would be affected by such changes.
the triple-alpha process has an intrinsic tolerance against changes of the fundamental constants of the order of 3%, and that it is not possible to exclude that the process is more robust.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a fundamental question of physics: How do the fundamental constants of Nature influence the evolution of our Universe?
the sensitivity of a fundamental nuclear physics reaction, the triple-alpha process, to variations in the fundamental constants of Nature.
the interplay between the fundamental constants of physics, the structure of nuclei, and the emergence of complex systems in the Universe.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the physics of life is not in jeopardy due to the variation of the fundamental constants of Nature.
the anthropic principle is not needed to explain the existence of life in our Universe.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sensitivity of the triple-alpha reaction to the fundamental constants is much weaker than previously thought.
we find no evidence for a strong dependence of the triple-alpha rate on the fundamental constants, which is in contrast to the results from a recent study by Berezhiani and Pospelov (2013).
the triple-alpha process appears to be robust against variations in the fundamental parameters of the theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the triple-alpha process can be expected to work in most of the parameter space allowed by present experimental constraints.
the production rate of the elements carbon and oxygen in the Universe is robust with respect to variations of the light quark mass and electromagnetic coupling.
the production of the most abundant elements in the Universe is robust against variations of the fundamental parameters of the Standard Model of Particle Physics.
